title: High School Students’ Discursive Routines in the Context of Linear Equations
text_snippet: High School Students’ Discursive Routines in the Context of Linear Equations Purpose: This case study explores the discursive routines of three 11th-grade students from a public high school as they engaged with single-variable linear equations. Specifically, it aims to reveal the nature and structure of their participation in mathematical discourse and to examine how their algebraic understanding of linear equations is constructed from a commognitive perspective. Method: A qualitative case study design was employed. Data were collected via semi-structured individual interviews, lasting between 40 and 60 minutes, and recorded using two cameras to capture the students’ mathematical communication in detail. The analysis focused on how students participated in mathematical discourse, particularly using ritual and exploration routines. Findings: The findings reveal that students mainly relied on ritual routines, concentrating on performing rigid procedures rather than producing mathematical narratives. Their discourse centered on calculations, treating equations as sequences of symbols to manipulate rather than as mathematical objects. title: High School Teachers’ Views On the Utilization of 21st Century Learner And Teacher Skills
text_snippet: High School Teachers’ Views On the Utilization of 21st Century Learner And Teacher Skills Purpose: The aim of this study is to determine the views of high school teachers on their use of 21st-century learner and teacher skills. Method: A case study design was employed in the research. The study group consists of 35 teachers working in high school institutions, selected through maximum variation sampling. A semi-structured interview form developed by the researchers was used as the data collection tool. In the analysis of the data obtained, content analysis and descriptive analysis were performed using NVivo 15 software. Findings: According to the results, high school teachers categorized 21st-century learning skills as "cognitive", "autonomous", "collaboration and flexibility", and "innovativeness" skills. Teachers stated that possessing 21st-century learning skills contributes to individuals in affective, social, and cognitive domains. Additionally, they perceived 21st-century teacher skills as consisting of cognitive skills, literacy skills, and social, affective, and psychomotor skills. title: Examining the Pedagogical Content Knowledge of Mathematics Teacher Candidates on Cone Subject Regarding Students’ Mistakes
text_snippet: Examining the Pedagogical Content Knowledge of Mathematics Teacher Candidates on Cone Subject Regarding Students’ Mistakes Purpose: This research aims to examine the pedagogical content knowledge of fourth-grade mathematics teacher candidates regarding the concept of the cone, based on knowledge of student understanding and knowledge of instructional strategies. Method: The study sample consists of 51 fourth-grade mathematics teacher candidates. The Pedagogical Content Knowledge Test and semi-structured interviews were used as data collection tools. The test was administered to 51 mathematics teacher candidates, and interviews were conducted with six of them. Findings: The study revealed that the mathematics teacher candidates had deficiencies in both knowledge of student understanding and knowledge of instructional strategies. In terms of knowledge of student understanding, it was observed that some mathematics teacher candidates did not include cone types other than the right circular cone in the cone group, did not consider the hierarchical relationship between cones and pyramids, and had incomplete knowledge regarding the open form and area-volume formulas of a cone. title: Preschool Teachers’ Competencies for Organizing Out-of-School Learning: A Multivariate Analysis
text_snippet: Preschool Teachers’ Competencies for Organizing Out-of-School Learning: A Multivariate Analysis Purpose: The effective implementation of out-of-school learning (OOSL) activities requires that teachers possess the necessary competencies to plan, implement, and assess learning in such environments. The present study aims to examine preschool teachers’ competency levels in organizing out-of-school learning and to investigate whether these competencies differ according to gender, professional seniority, and educational background. Method: The research was carried out in the spring term of the 2023–2024 academic year and involved 147 preschool teachers employed in a provincial city situated in Türkiye's Central Anatolia Region. Data collection tools included a demographic information form and the Organizing OOSL Scale. Alongside descriptive statistics, the dataset was analyzed through MANOVA and multiple regression techniques. Findings: Findings indicated that teachers generally demonstrated high competency levels in organizing OOSL activities. However, when examined across sub-dimensions, the lowest mean scores were observed in the “knowledge” dimension, especially in areas related to legal regulations and safety procedures. title: Mapping Computational Thinking Research in Early Childhood Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of Explicitly CT-Labelled Literature
text_snippet: Mapping Computational Thinking Research in Early Childhood Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of Explicitly CT-Labelled Literature Purpose: Computational thinking (CT) has increasingly been recognized as a foundational competence within early childhood education (ECE). Although the volume of research has grown, limited attention has been given to how different research traditions shape the development of CT in ECE. This study aims to examine the structural evolution of CT research in ECE and to identify dominant themes, research trends, and underexplored areas in the literature. Method: A bibliometric analysis was conducted on 210 peer-reviewed articles published between 2011 and August 2025 and indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection. Using Biblioshiny, publication trends, influential contributors, and thematic structures were analyzed to map the intellectual development of CT research in ECE. Findings: The findings indicate a rapid increase in CT research after 2017, reflecting its transition from a niche topic to an emerging and increasingly recognized area of scholarly inquiry. However, this growth remains geographically concentrated within a limited number of regional contexts. title: The Effect of Video-Supported Exercises Based on Repetition Strategy in Cello Instruction on Performing Turkish Music Makam Scales
text_snippet: The Effect of Video-Supported Exercises Based on Repetition Strategy in Cello Instruction on Performing Turkish Music Makam Scales Purpose: This study aims to determine the effectiveness of video-supported applications based on the repetition strategy in cello instruction on students' performance levels of Turkish music makam scales and to explore their experiences. Method: An action research design utilizing both qualitative and quantitative data types was adopted with five cello students. Data were collected through researcher and student journals, and peşrev evaluation forms. The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test was used for quantitative analysis. Qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis, and inter-coder reliability was established with Cohen's Kappa coefficient (.915 for researcher journals, .935 for student journals). Findings: Quantitative results revealed a statistically significant (p 0.90) across all analyzed makams. title: Understanding the Mathematical Problem Through Two Comprehension Strategies
text_snippet: Understanding the Mathematical Problem Through Two Comprehension Strategies Purpose: This article discusses two strategies, underlining key information and identifying the givens and the unknowns, within a teaching module developed to improve students’ problem comprehension skills. The aim of the study was to examine changes in students’ problem-understanding behaviors following teaching sessions incorporating these strategies. Method: The main study was designed as a qualitative teaching experiment; however, this article presents a case study focusing specifically on these two strategies. Four different question forms were used to determine students’ problem-comprehension behaviors before and after the teaching sessions. Findings: Prior to the intervention, students spent less time understanding the problem than solving it and demonstrated limited use of problem-comprehension strategies. Following the teaching sessions, an increase was observed in students’ use of these strategies. A considerable number of students were able to understand the problems and formulate appropriate solution strategies. title: An Investigation of Science Teacher Candidates' Context-Based Question Writing Skills
text_snippet: An Investigation of Science Teacher Candidates' Context-Based Question Writing Skills Purpose: Developments in education and teaching activities in the 21st century have transformed student roles, positioning students as individuals who critically evaluate, question knowledge, and apply it in daily life and problem-solving. The PISA exam, which assesses skills in various domains, stands out in determining whether students have acquired these competencies. Teachers play a crucial role in providing students with opportunities to gain these skills and in evaluating their progress. The first step in achieving the targeted educational standards is the training of teacher candidates. Therefore, equipping teacher candidates with the ability to create context-based texts and formulate questions appropriate to the context is of great importance. Based on this premise, this study aims to thoroughly examine the context-based question-writing skills of science teacher candidates. Method: The study was conducted using a case study design, one of the qualitative research methods. The participants consisted of 34 science teacher candidates. title: Evaluating Early Childhood Classroom Environments: A Mixed-Methods Comparison of Teacher Perceptions and Classroom Practices
text_snippet: Evaluating Early Childhood Classroom Environments: A Mixed-Methods Comparison of Teacher Perceptions and Classroom Practices Purpose: This study aimed to evaluate the early childhood classroom environment. In this context, teachers’ perspectives on early childhood classroom settings were gathered, and the teachers were observed regarding their experiences during the instructional process. Method: The study employed an explanatory sequential design, one of the mixed research methods. Data were collected through the “Early Childhood Classroom Environment Assessment Scale” and unstructured observation form. Responses were obtained from 224 teachers using the scale, and observations were conducted in the classrooms of 21 teachers. Descriptive statistics, such as mean and standard deviation, were used for analyzing the quantitative data, while content analysis was applied to analyze the qualitative data. Findings: The findings revealed that the teachers reported supporting problem-solving, providing effective feedback, creating a high-quality classroom environment, encouraging positive behavior, and fostering self-efficacy. title: Concrete Materials in the Teaching of Geometric Solids: Availability and Usage in Middle Schools
text_snippet: Concrete Materials in the Teaching of Geometric Solids: Availability and Usage in Middle Schools Purpose: This study aimed to examine middle school mathematics teachers’ use of concrete materials in the teaching of geometric solids and to determine the availability of such materials in schools. Method: A descriptive research design was employed. The participants were 25 mathematics teachers working in middle schools in a city in Türkiye’s Southeastern Anatolia Region, selected through a combination of stratified purposeful sampling and criterion sampling. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistical methods and qualitative content analysis. Findings: The findings revealed that most concrete materials suitable for teaching geometric solids were not available in schools. Teachers predominantly used available materials, while alternative strategies, such as using handmade or student-made models, providing real-life examples, and employing interactive whiteboards, were adopted when concrete materials were unavailable. Most teachers did not express views regarding the reasons for material shortages. title: The Effect of Practice-Based Special Education Activities on Preservice Teachers’ Self-Efficacy Perceptions
text_snippet: The Effect of Practice-Based Special Education Activities on Preservice Teachers’ Self-Efficacy Perceptions Purpose: The increasing implementation of inclusive education in Türkiye highlights the need to strengthen preservice teachers’ competencies in educating individuals with special educational needs. Practice-based learning experiences integrated into undergraduate special education and inclusion courses play a critical role in enhancing preservice teachers’ self-efficacy beliefs. This study aims to examine the effect of expert-designed special education and inclusive education activities on preservice teachers’ self-efficacy. Method: A single-group pretest–posttest quasi-experimental design was employed. The participants were 169 preservice teachers enrolled in a faculty of education at a public university. Data was collected using the Teacher Self-Efficacy Scale for the Education of Individuals with Special Needs. Descriptive statistics and 2×2 and 2×5 mixed-design ANOVA were used for data analysis. Findings: Preservice teachers’ self-efficacy scores increased significantly after the implementation. The main effect of time was significant across all analyses. title: The Visibility of Kitchen and Cleaning Staff Working in Preschool Education Institutions
text_snippet: The Visibility of Kitchen and Cleaning Staff Working in Preschool Education Institutions Purpose: This research aims to understand the social visibility of kitchen and cleaning staff working in preschools. Method: The research was conducted using basic qualitative research methods. Maximum variation sampling was used to determine the study group, which consisted of a total of 21 people: 5 kitchen staff, 11 cleaning staff, and 5 administrators. Data were collected from the study group through semi-structured interviews, and the data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The research theoretically examined visibility through socio-cultural (the ways in which culture and society influence visibility), socio-legal (the legal and regulatory factors affecting visibility), and socio-spatial (the physical and spatial aspects of visibility) mechanisms. The themes were named after these mechanisms. Coding and categorization processes were conducted based on visibility. Findings: The research findings demonstrate that kitchen and cleaning staff maintain clear socio-cultural and socio-spatial visibility within preschool settings. title: The Use of Video-Assisted Feedback in University-Level English Language Teaching: A Systematic Review
text_snippet: The Use of Video-Assisted Feedback in University-Level English Language Teaching: A Systematic Review Purpose: This research aims to examine the effectiveness of video-assisted feedback use in university-level English language teaching (ELT) classes based on the results of the studies in the field. Method: The research was carried out within the framework of Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). For this purpose, Web of Science (WoS) was searched by using the keywords “video-based feedback”, “video-assisted feedback”, “video feedback”. In the selection phase, the studies were evaluated according to their contents, and the studies that met the inclusion criteria and were suitable for the research purpose were included in the systematic review. A total of 16 studies from 2015 to 2025 were included in the study. Findings: The findings show that video-assisted feedback has positive impact on the achievement and language proficiency of students. Moreover, when video-assisted feedback was used, students were reported to show positive progress regarding their motivation, anxiety, attitude, reflection, self-efficacy, self-confidence, and responsibility. title: Social Studies Teacher Candidates’ Perceptions of the Concept of Artificial Intelligence: A Metaphor Analysis
text_snippet: Social Studies Teacher Candidates’ Perceptions of the Concept of Artificial Intelligence: A Metaphor Analysis Purpose: This study aims to examine the perceptions of social studies teacher candidates regarding the concept of artificial intelligence through the metaphors they generate. By revealing teacher candidates’ mental representations of artificial intelligence, the study seeks to contribute to a better understanding of their perceptions and to provide an original perspective for teacher education and the literature. Method: A qualitative research approach based on a phenomenological design was employed. The study group consisted of 128 social studies teacher candidates enrolled at a public university in Türkiye during the fall semester of the 2025–2026 academic year. Participants were selected on a voluntary basis using convenience sampling. Data were collected through a form including personal information questions and the prompt, “Artificial intelligence is like … because ….” The metaphors produced by the participants constituted the primary data source and were analyzed using qualitative content analysis. title: Latent Profile Analysis of Cyberbullying, Depression, and Social Support Among Turkish Adolescents: Role of Demographic Characteristics
text_snippet: Latent Profile Analysis of Cyberbullying, Depression, and Social Support Among Turkish Adolescents: Role of Demographic Characteristics Purpose: Cyberbullying is a significant threat to adolescent well-being, yet most research has used variable-centered approaches that fail to capture the complex interplay of behaviors and psychosocial factors. A person-centered approach is needed to identify how these factors cluster together within distinct subgroups of adolescents. The aim of the study is to identify distinct psychosocial profiles among Turkish adolescents by exploring how cyberbullying behaviors (cyber victimization, bullying) cluster together with psychosocial factors (depression and perceived social support). Method: The study utilized Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) on a sample of 592 Turkish adolescents. Findings: The results of the study yielded three distinct profiles: a large uninvolved (low-risk) group, a bully (perpetration-focused) group and a bully-victim (high-risk) group. The analysis revealed the critical protective influence of perceived social support and the significant risk associated with depression. title: The Relationship Between Climate Change, Migration and Education for the NBR of The Gambia.
text_snippet: The Relationship Between Climate Change, Migration and Education for the NBR of The Gambia. Purpose: Climate change–related extreme events have compelled many people to leave their homes in search of safer and more favourable environments. At the same time, migration linked to climate shocks continues to rise as these events become more frequent and intense worldwide. This study analyses the relationships between climate change, migration, and education in The Gambia, addressing a notable research gap in this context. Method: Structured household questionnaires were used to collect data, and Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) was applied to establish relationships among the three constructs. Findings: The findings suggest that as climate change intensifies, migration rates decrease. However, there is a positive relationship between migration and education, indicating that individuals with higher educational attainment are more likely to migrate. Conclusion: The study highlights the pressing need for climate adaptation strategies, enhanced access to education, and socioeconomic reforms to address the challenges of climate-induced migration. title: Motivational Factors Influencing Academic Staff Participation in Erasmus+ Staff Mobility for Teaching Assignments (STA)
text_snippet: Motivational Factors Influencing Academic Staff Participation in Erasmus+ Staff Mobility for Teaching Assignments (STA) Purpose: This study examines the motivational factors shaping academic staff participation in the Erasmus+ Staff Mobility for Teaching Assignments program through a qualitative inquiry conducted at a public university in Türkiye. Method: Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with academic staff who had previously participated in the program and were analyzed in MAXQDA using reflexive thematic analysis. The analysis focused on how participants described the personal, institutional, and structural conditions shaping their mobility decisions. Findings: The findings show that participants primarily associated participation with establishing and sustaining international academic collaborations, acquiring and sharing international experience, enriching teaching practices, and broadening their international outlook. Institutional facilitation, procedural clarity, and supportive organizational conditions also appeared among the factors encouraging participation. title: Secondary Traumatic Stress and Music Activity Preferences After The 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquake
text_snippet: Secondary Traumatic Stress and Music Activity Preferences After The 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquake Purpose: This study aims to examine the relationship between secondary traumatic stress (STS) related to social media content about the 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquake and the music activity preferences (e.g., listening, playing, singing) of education faculty students. Modifying music consumption is explored as a potential emotion regulation strategy associated with coping with vicarious trauma. Method: A quantitative correlational screening model was employed. The study group consisted of 278 undergraduate education faculty students in Türkiye. Data were collected during the 2022-2023 Spring Semester using the Secondary Traumatic Stress Scale for Social Media Users and a researcher-developed Music Activities Preference Form. Data were analyzed using independent samples t-tests and Chi-square tests. Findings: Students who changed their music preferences post-earthquake exhibited significantly higher STS scores compared to those who did not (p<0.001, Cohen's d=0.49). Significant associations were found between pre- and post-earthquake music genres (p<0.001, Cramer's V=0.60) , as well as the emotional characteristics of the melodic (p<0.001, Cramer's V=0.40) and lyrical structures (p<0

journal_name: Bartin University Journal of Faculty of Education
title: The Relationship Between 7th and 8th Grade Students' Scientific Creativity Levels and Their Attitudes Toward Science Course and Laboratory Applications
text_snippet: The Relationship Between 7th and 8th Grade Students' Scientific Creativity Levels and Their Attitudes Toward Science Course and Laboratory Applications Purpose: This study was conducted to determine the relationship between the scientific creativity levels of seventh and eighth-grade students and their attitudes towards science courses and laboratory applications. Method: The research sample consists of 341 students in the 7th and 8th grades at three middle schools in the Battalgazi district of Malatya province. To determine students' scientific creativity levels, the Scientific Creativity Test (SCT), developed by Hu and Adey (2012) and adapted into Turkish by Deniş and Balım (2012), was applied. To measure students' attitudes towards science and technology courses, the “Science and Technology Attitude Scale (STAS),” prepared by Keçeci and Zengin (2015), was used. To assess their attitudes towards science and technology laboratories, the “Science Laboratory Applications Attitude Scale (SLAAS),” developed by El-Gendy and adapted to science laboratories by Yeşilyurt (2003), was implemented. title: Creative Self-Regulation Scale: Adaptation, Validity, and Reliability Study
text_snippet: Creative Self-Regulation Scale: Adaptation, Validity, and Reliability Study Purpose: The aim of this study is to adapt the Creative Self-Regulation Scale, developed to determine students' self-regulation skills in creative projects, to Turkish culture. Method: Following the translation process suggested by Hambleton et al. (2005), initial translation, back-translation, and final checks were performed. Foreign language, science, and measurement-evaluation experts evaluated the scale according to the adaptation stages, and the scale was finalized. A survey design of quantitative research was used in the study. The translated scale was administered to 167 high school students. Findings: Exploratory factor analysis yielded a three-factor structure consisting of 25 items explaining 45.34% of the variance, and this structure was confirmed by confirmatory factor analysis. After validity checks, Cronbach's alpha and composite reliability coefficients were calculated to check the reliability of the scale, and it was determined that the reliability coefficients were greater than 0.70 for both the overall scale and the sub-factors. title: Examining Attention Control in Pre-service EFL Teachers: Effects of A Mindfulness-Based Intervention
text_snippet: Examining Attention Control in Pre-service EFL Teachers: Effects of A Mindfulness-Based Intervention Purpose: In today's digital world, students often struggle with short attention spans, constant distractions, and high levels of stress. Hence, this study aimed to investigate the impact of mindfulness practices on the English Language Teaching (ELT) pre-service teachers’ (PTs) mindfulness and attention control in a state university in Türkiye. Method: Following a mixed-methods approach with a pre-experimental design, 81 ELT PTs were administered the Freiburg Mindfulness Inventory and the Attention Control Scale before and after the 12-week mindfulness-based intervention, in addition to employing an open-ended questionnaire. Findings: A paired sample t-test results revealed a significant increase in general mindfulness and a highly significant improvement in attention control, suggesting that the intervention enhanced the PTs’ attention control. title: Cognitive Performance in the Dominant Language: A Comparison of Bilingual and Monolingual Adults on Executive and Lexical Tasks
text_snippet: Cognitive Performance in the Dominant Language: A Comparison of Bilingual and Monolingual Adults on Executive and Lexical Tasks Purpose: This study examines the effects of bilingual experience and age of acquisition on executive control and lexical performance in the dominant language. A total of 23 adults participated, including early bilinguals (Kurdish/Arabic–Turkish), late bilinguals (Turkish–English), and Turkish monolinguals. Method: Participants completed a color-naming Stroop task to assess inhibitory control and a vocabulary task in Turkish to measure lexical retrieval. Findings: Non-parametric analyses revealed that early bilinguals significantly outperformed both late bilinguals and monolinguals in the incongruent condition of the Stroop task, indicating enhanced executive control. In contrast, no significant differences were found among the three groups in vocabulary performance in Turkish. Conclusion: These findings suggest that early and sustained bilingual exposure may confer advantages in executive functioning, whereas lexical performance in the dominant language appears less sensitive to bilingual experience under conditions of similar language exposure. title: An Examination of the Relationship between Aggression and Sociometric Popularity in Preschool Children
text_snippet: An Examination of the Relationship between Aggression and Sociometric Popularity in Preschool Children Purpose: Aggression is an increasingly prevalent behavioral problem today. Studies show that aggression can harm children's social relationships, increasing their likelihood of exposure to peer violence and rejection by their peers. Aggressive children are more likely to inflict violence on their peers and are more likely to be exposed to their violence. This study aimed to determine the linear and curvilinear relationships between sociometric popularity and aggression in children. Method: The study group consisted of 420 children aged 5-6 years. Relationships between variables were analyzed using correlation. The effects of gender on aggression and popularity in girls and boys were tested using an independent samples t-test. Then, linear regression analysis and second-order regression analysis were performed, respectively, to determine the effects between the variables. Findings: Aggression scores were found to be higher in boys, while sociometric popularity scores were higher in girls. title: Trends and Methodological Features of Engineering Design-Based Science Education Research in Turkey
text_snippet: Trends and Methodological Features of Engineering Design-Based Science Education Research in Turkey Purpose: It is essential to elevate the levels of awareness and consciousness among individuals within society to keep pace with the rapid changes and advancements in science and technology, such transformations can only be achieved through education and instruction. In today’s world, traditional teaching methods have been replaced by approaches which are better suited to contemporary conditions. Changes in our education programs are now evident through methods such as problem-based learning, inquiry-based learning, peer instruction, project-based learning, and STEM education. Recently, efforts have been made to integrate engineering design-based science education (EDBSE) within STEM education. Studies investigating this integration have shown that this approach has positive effects on teachers, prospective teachers, and students. The data for this research consists of 55 full-text scientific research articles on EDBSE published electronically in Turkey between 2015 and 2024. Method: In the study, document analysis-a qualitative research method-was conducted. Content analysis was employed to analyze the research data, and a publication classification form was used. title: An Attempt at Text Modification Within the Framework of Text Linguistic Criteria for Teaching Turkish to Foreigners: Rıfat Ilgaz-Şeker Kutusu
text_snippet: An Attempt at Text Modification Within the Framework of Text Linguistic Criteria for Teaching Turkish to Foreigners: Rıfat Ilgaz-Şeker Kutusu Purpose: This study aims to contribute to the field of Teaching Turkish as a Foreign Language (TTFL) by adapting Rıfat Ilgaz’s short story Şeker Kutusu to the A2 proficiency level within the framework of text linguistic criteria. Method: The study employs qualitative research design using document analysis. The selected literary text was analyzed based on CEFR descriptors, the European Language Portfolio and text linguistic principles. Findings: The adaptation process included lexical simplification, syntactic restructuring, and clarification of complex expressions while preserving narrative coherence. The findings indicate that the adapted text supports comprehension and vocabulary development at the A2 level. Conclusion: The study demonstrates that literary texts can be systematically adapted according to linguistic criteria without losing their literary value, thereby making them accessible to beginner learners.

title: Assessment of Argumentation and Proof-Based Mathematics Instruction
text_snippet: Assessment of Argumentation and Proof-Based Mathematics Instruction Purpose: One of the fundamental goals of educational systems is to cultivate individuals who are capable of accessing information and critically evaluating its accuracy. The ability to engage in logical reasoning and to present arguments coherently and persuasively has become an increasingly essential competency in the current societal context. This study aims to examine students’ argumentation schemes, proof schemes, and their perspectives within the context of Argumentation and Proof-Based Mathematics Instruction. Method: A qualitative research design was employed to explore the impact of Argumentation and Proof-Based Mathematics Instruction (APBMI). The study was conducted with 30 sixth-grade students in Kayseri, Türkiye. To conduct a detailed analysis of qualitative data, 12 students were selected from among the thirty students and interviewed. A 20-hour instructional program was designed and implemented over six weeks. Findings: Based on the analysis of students’ responses, two levels of argumentation quality, “demonstrate an acceptable level of argumentation quality” and “demonstrate a good level of argumentation quality,” were identified. title: Mapping Research Trends on Curriculum Literacy and Social Emotional Learning in Teacher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis
text_snippet: Mapping Research Trends on Curriculum Literacy and Social Emotional Learning in Teacher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis Purpose: This study presents a bibliometric mapping of research on curriculum literacy and social emotional learning (SEL) in teacher education. Rather than examining empirical effects or causal relationships, the study aims to identify publication trends, collaboration patterns, and the intellectual structure of the field. Method: Using the Web of Science (WoS) database, 85 publications published between 2019 and 2024 were analyzed through bibliometric techniques. Data were examined using VOSviewer to visualize co-authorship networks, co-citation structures, and keyword co-occurrence patterns. Findings: The findings reveal a growing scholarly interest in SEL and curriculum literacy, with increasing publication and citation trends, dominant research clusters, and strong international collaboration networks. The bibliometric maps highlight key thematic concentrations, influential authors, and emerging subtopics that shape the current research landscape. title: How Can We Visualize Mathematical Concepts Outside the Box? Tracing the Journey from Formal Definitions to Inventive “Pictures of Mathematical Concepts”
text_snippet: How Can We Visualize Mathematical Concepts Outside the Box? Tracing the Journey from Formal Definitions to Inventive “Pictures of Mathematical Concepts” Purpose: Visualization offers the opportunity to represent the features of mathematical concepts and the relationships between mathematical concepts in various forms. This study aimed to examine the visualization process of mathematical concepts of preservice mathematics teachers (PMTs). Method: The study employed a qualitative method. All participants were given formal definitions of mathematical concepts and asked to draw pictures of them. They attempted to visualize the features and relationships of concepts with the help of drawing and painting. Discussions were carried out in the classroom about whether the pictures were appropriate in terms of representing the concepts visually. Following these discussions, interviews were conducted with the groups whose pictures were deemed suitable by the class to represent the concept visually. The pictures and views of the PMTs regarding the visualization process of the concepts were analyzed through the techniques of the grounded theory method. title: The Century of Türkiye Education Model's Reflection on English Language Teaching: Impacts on Students’ Self-Efficacy and Attitudes
text_snippet: The Century of Türkiye Education Model's Reflection on English Language Teaching: Impacts on Students’ Self-Efficacy and Attitudes This study aims to examine the associations between value-based and skills-oriented English activities, designed by the teacher and inspired by the student profile of the Century of Türkiye Education Model (CTEM) and the virtue-value-action framework, and students’ perceptions of English self-efficacy and their attitudes towards the course. Designed as an exploratory case study, the research employed a mixed-methods approach, incorporating both quantitative and qualitative data. A total of 18 students enrolled in a 12th-grade English language class participated in a six-week intervention process in which teacher-designed English activities were implemented based on selected principles of the CTEM student profile. Data were collected through pre- and post-intervention self-efficacy and attitude scales, as well as an online written form and reflective responses via digital tools. The results showed statistically significant increases in students’ self-efficacy scores across all four language skills, with the largest mean change observed in speaking. title: The Collapse of Graduate Dreams: Motivational Dynamics and Difficulties Experienced by Teachers Who Dropped Out of Postgraduate Education
text_snippet: The Collapse of Graduate Dreams: Motivational Dynamics and Difficulties Experienced by Teachers Who Dropped Out of Postgraduate Education The purpose of this study is to identify the sources of motivation of teachers who did not complete their graduate education before starting their department and how motivation decreased over time. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with sixteen teachers who dropped out of graduate education during the 2023-2024 academic year at four different universities in Turkey. The criterion sampling method was used to determine the study group. The data were analyzed using content analysis. Findings from the study, conducted using a qualitative approach and case study design, revealed that teachers initially began graduate education motivated primarily by professional development, desire for management, status acquisition, breaking monotony, and overcoming feelings of professional inadequacy. However, during the thesis phase, it was determined that structural problems such as physical and mental fatigue, time constraints, the oppressive attitude of advisors, and lack of guidance seriously undermined motivation. title: The Relationship Between Preservice Teachers’ Level of Innovativeness and Academic Career Awareness
text_snippet: The Relationship Between Preservice Teachers’ Level of Innovativeness and Academic Career Awareness Purpose: The purpose of this study is to examine the relationship between preservice teachers’ levels of individual innovativeness and their awareness of academic careers. Method: The research employed a correlational survey model with a sample of 333 preservice teachers enrolled in the Faculty of Education of a university in the Black Sea Region of Türkiye during the 2024-2025 academic year. Data were collected using the Individual Innovativeness Scale and the Academic Career Awareness Scale. Findings: The findings indicated that preservice teachers demonstrated a moderate level of individual innovativeness, with the highest mean score observed in the “resistance to change” dimension and the lowest in “risk-taking.” Preservice teachers’ overall academic career awareness levels were found to be high, with the strongest awareness in the dimension of “being a faculty member and related conditions.” Correlation analysis revealed a low but statistically significant positive relationship between individual innovativeness and academic career awareness. title: Instructional Leadership in a Centralized Education System: Revisiting the Practice of School Principals
text_snippet: Instructional Leadership in a Centralized Education System: Revisiting the Practice of School Principals Purpose: This study examines teachers’ and school administrators’ views on principals’ instructional leadership roles and the effects of these roles on educational processes. Method: Within the framework of a qualitative phenomenological research design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 20 participants and analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings: The findings indicate that instructional leadership practices are concentrated in three main domains: defining the school mission, managing instructional processes, and developing learning environments. Participants emphasized that principals support instructional practices, foster a positive school climate, and strengthen student-centered learning approaches. Instructional leadership was found to produce multilevel effects, including the strengthening of organizational culture at the school level, the enhancement of teacher motivation and professional development at the teacher level, and the improvement of learning outcomes at the student level. title: Mapping the Research Landscape of Teacher Mindset: A Bibliometric Analysis (1984–2024)
text_snippet: Mapping the Research Landscape of Teacher Mindset: A Bibliometric Analysis (1984–2024) Research on teacher mindset has expanded considerably over the past decades, reflecting growing interest in its theoretical and pedagogical implications. Nevertheless, limited attention has been given to systematically mapping the field’s intellectual structure and thematic evolution through an integrative bibliometric approach. This study was conducted to reveal the intellectual structure, scientific evolution and thematic transformation of the teacher mindset literature. A total of 335 eligible publications between 1984 and 2024 obtained from the Web of Science Core Collection database were evaluated through quantitative and visual bibliometric analysis techniques employing Biblioshiny and VOSviewer software. The analysis reveals that the field has gained significant momentum in the post-2007 period, scientific productivity has been steadily increasing annually, and literature is largely shaped around the concepts of growth mindset and implicit theories. The deviations observed in the productivity analysis based on Lotka's Law reveal that teacher mindset research has not yet reached academic maturity, in other words, there is potential for expansion in this field. title: Investigating Self-Efficacy of English Student Teachers’ Intercultural Communication
text_snippet: Investigating Self-Efficacy of English Student Teachers’ Intercultural Communication Purpose: Psychological, characteristic and socio-cultural factors are effective in shaping perceptions of self-efficacy in communicating in intercultural encounters. Therefore, using an explanatory study, the present research investigates the self-efficacy of 194 (CFA and main study sample) and 133 (EFA sample) student teachers of English in intercultural communication. Method: In the study, quantitative data were collected with the adopted version of the Self-Efficacy in Communication Scale (SEFFICAC) to investigate the participants' characteristics in intercultural communication. Qualitative data were collected with an interview form consisting of written, structured questions. The extent to which student teachers of English find themselves competent in intercultural communication was analysed in depth. Findings: The qualitative data obtained in the study showed that the student teachers of English who participated in the study rarely experienced intercultural encounters, found themselves competent in intercultural communication situations, and were open and willing to intercultural communication. title: Examination of Illustrated Children's Books on Natural Disasters
text_snippet: Examination of Illustrated Children's Books on Natural Disasters This study was conducted to examine illustrated children's books on natural disasters prepared for the early childhood period. To this end, a document review was conducted using criterion sampling, one of the purposive sampling methods, to determine the study group. Accordingly, 20 illustrated children's books were included in the study, and the “Illustrated Children's Books on Natural Disasters Evaluation Form” prepared by the researchers in accordance with the relevant literature was used in the examination of these books. Through this form, the books in the study group were examined under a total of four themes: physical, drawing, content, and language characteristics. The research data was coded using content analysis methods to create categories, and examples were presented in tables. According to the study findings, the physical features theme consisted of the categories of cover, design, dimensions, typography, target age group, and illustrations. title: The Impact of Argumentation-Based Environmental Education on the Environmental Literacy of Pre-service Science Teachers
text_snippet: The Impact of Argumentation-Based Environmental Education on the Environmental Literacy of Pre-service Science Teachers Purpose: This study investigates the impact of argumentation-based environmental education on the development of environmental literacy among pre-service science teachers (PSTs) using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. Method: A total of 55 PSTs were divided into experimental (n=28) and comparison (n=27) groups. Over a seven-week period, the experimental group received scenario-based argumentation instruction on environmental issues, while the comparison group followed a traditional instructional approach. Quantitative data were collected using the “Environmental Literacy Scale”, and qualitative data were gathered through semi-structured interviews. Findings: Independent samples t-tests revealed that the experimental group demonstrated significantly higher gains in environmental knowledge (t(53)=4.86, p<0.001), environmental attitude (t(53)=2.97, p< 0.01), and environmental use (t(53)=2.85, p< 0.01) compared to the comparison group. title: The Evaluation of High School Students' Tendencies and Opinions Regarding E-Diseases
text_snippet: The Evaluation of High School Students' Tendencies and Opinions Regarding E-Diseases Purpose: The primary aim of this study is to determine high school students’ tendencies toward digitally based e-disorders such as selfitis, cheesepodding, photolurking, FoMO (fear of missing out), and Facebook depression, as well as their levels of knowledge regarding these conditions. Method: A mixed-method research design was employed in the study. The sample consisted of 480 students enrolled in three different types of high schools (Anatolian, Vocational, and Imam Hatip high schools) located in the Çaldıran district of Van province. Maximum variation sampling was utilized to ensure the inclusion of diverse perspectives and conditions. Quantitative data were collected through the “E-Disorder Tendency Determination Questionnaire,” while qualitative data were obtained via a semi-structured interview form. Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS 23, and qualitative data were analyzed using MAXQDA 24. Findings: The findings revealed that both female and male students attending Anatolian, Vocational, and Imam Hatip high schools exhibited low levels of tendency toward selfitis, cheesepodding, photolurking, FoMO (fear of missing out), and Facebook depression. The Example of Eymen and Çimen for Preschoolers The purpose of this research is to examine the cartoon "Eymen and Çimen" in terms of gender stereotypes. This study employed a qualitative research approach. The study group comprised all published episodes of the cartoon "Eymen and Çimen. A checklist developed by the researchers was used as the data collection tool, and descriptive analysis was employed for data analysis. During the data analysis, the number of characters, personality traits, toy and clothing choices in the cartoon were examined, and the colors used in the cartoon were generally evaluated. It was observed that there were more female characters than male characters in the cartoon, but the main character was male. The male character's room and clothing were predominantly blue, while the female characters were pink. In terms of personality traits, female characters were attributed characteristics such as calm and nurturing, while male characters were attributed characteristics such as adventurous and anxious. Gender differences were identified in play and toy selection. The male character's room was found to contain gender-specific toys such as cars, Legos, trucks, and airplanes. title: Playing-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders and Mental Well-Being Among Music Students
text_snippet: Playing-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders and Mental Well-Being Among Music Students This mixed-methods study investigates the interplay between playing-related musculoskeletal disorders (PRMDs) and mental well-being among undergraduate music students in Türkiye. Quantitatively, PRMDs were assessed with the Cornell Musculoskeletal Discomfort Questionnaire (CMDQ) and mental well-being with the Short Warwick–Edinburgh Mental Well-Being Scale (SWEMWBS), alongside demographics and practice-behavior variables; descriptive statistics and non-parametric tests were employed. Qualitatively, open-ended responses were examined via thematic analysis. Findings indicate that PRMDs cluster predominantly in the upper back, neck, and lower back, with string and keyboard players reporting higher discomfort. Single practice sessions exceeding 90 minutes were associated with significantly greater PRMD severity, whereas regular micro-breaks related to lower discomfort. A moderate negative correlation emerged between CMDQ totals and SWEMWBS scores (ρ≈–.41, p<.01). title: A Descriptive Content Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Studies with Primary and Pre-Service Primary School Teachers in Türkiye
text_snippet: A Descriptive Content Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Studies with Primary and Pre-Service Primary School Teachers in Türkiye In this study, academic studies on artificial intelligence (AI) conducted with primary school teachers and pre-service primary school teachers in Türkiye were examined to determine current research trends. A descriptive content analysis method was employed including full-text accessible, Türkiye-affiliated studies retrieved from the National Thesis Centre (YÖKTEZ) and Google Scholar using AI and teacher-related keywords. A total of 25 studies, including 8 postgraduate theses and 17 journal articles, that met the predetermined criteria were analysed. The findings revealed a notable increase in research in recent years, with all theses conducted at the master's level. The most common research topics were participants’ views on AI, followed respectively by studies examining attitudes towards AI, AI literacy, AI anxiety, modelling with AI, and the effects of AI implementations. Methodologically, qualitative and quantitative approaches were used in nearly equal proportion, with survey and phenomenology designs being the most prominent.
